description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  Log::Log4perl is on the README's infrastructure list.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-hashderef-scalar.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    no strict "refs";
    my $x = 1;
    my $v = eval { $x->{a} };
    print "err=", ($@ ? "yes" : "no"), " v=", (defined $v ? $v : "undef"), "\n";

    use strict "refs";
    my $y = 1;
    my $w = eval { $y->{a} };
    print "strict err=", ($@ ? $@ : "none"), "\n";

    perl:  err=no v=undef
           strict err=Can't use string ("1") as a HASH ref while "strict refs"
                      in use at â¦ line 7.

    PCL :  err=yes v=undef                      <-- WRONG: perl does not die
           strict err=Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 1,
                      not a hash-table. at (eval 0) line 0.

TWO SEPARATE FAULTS IN ONE PLACE:

  (a) **Under `no strict refs` perl does NOT die.**  `$x->{a}` with `$x` = 1 is
      a SYMBOLIC reference â the hash `%main::1` â so the read is undef and the
      program continues.  PCL dies.  This is the one that costs rows.

  (b) Under `strict refs` both die, but PCL's message is a raw SBCL
      `simple-type-error` naming an internal (`pcl::h`, `sb-impl::gethash3`)
      instead of perl's "Can't use string (â¦) as a HASH ref while strict refs
      in use".  Per the memory note the exact TEXT is not a goal, but naming
      an SBCL internal in a user-visible error is a different thing from an
      imperfect wording, and rule 12 says the miss should say what it is.

WHAT IT COSTS, measured (s481b), Log-Log4perl-1.58-0's own suite:
PCL 13 PASS / 1 PARTIAL / 61 FAIL, 117 ok / 4 not-ok, against perl's 58 PASS
(and 17 files perl SKIPS itself â Log::Dispatch, DBI, XML::DOM, RRDs and
friends are absent, so the honest denominator is 58) with 752 ok / 0.  Sampled
files `t/002Logger.t`, `t/003Layout.t`, `t/004Config.t` all die at this exact
error and produce zero rows where perl produces 20-plus each.

(The `Can't locate loadable object for module this module` line these files
also print is NOISE, not the cause: it is `Sys::Hostname`'s
`eval { require XSLoader; XSLoader::load() }`, which perl also fails and warns
about, and PCL's eval catches it correctly â probed separately,
scratch/s481b/probe-xsloader-noargs.pl, hostname resolves on both sides.)

BAR: guard rows for `$x->{K}`, `$x->[0]`, `@$x`, `%$x`, `$$x` where `$x` holds a
number and a non-ref string, under BOTH pragma states, with perl as the oracle;
the `no strict refs` rows are reads AND writes (a write through a symbolic ref
creates the package variable in perl).
subject: A hash/array deref of a plain SCALAR dies with a raw SBCL type error (`Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 1, not a hash-table`) instead of perl's answer: under `no strict refs` perl treats it as a SYMBOLIC ref and returns undef, and under `strict refs` it dies with a named message.  It is the top cause of Log::Log4perl's suite (61 of 75 files FAIL).
